newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht weaker, interbank rate eases late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht weaker, interbank rate eases late.

text.p: The Thai baht edged down against the dollar in late trade on Monday on commercial demand for the dollar, dealers said.
"The baht was slightly weaker in the afternoon. The (baht/dollar) reference rate tomorrow is expected to be lower," said one dealer at a European bank.
The baht was quoted at around 28.90/29.00 to the dollar late in the domestic market compared with 28.650/28.950 in early morning trade.
The central bank announced the reference rate at 28.578 per dollar against 28.189 on Friday.
In the offshore market, the baht was traded at 28.50/28.80 against 28.50/29.10 in the morning.
Dealers said the central bank governor's comment on the expected level of the baht had no impact on the baht/dollar trade as the currency is now determined by market forces.
"I don't think the market takes the governor's comment into consideration. The demand and supply (of the dollar) is now the major factor (to affect the baht)," the dealer said.
Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Monday that he saw the baht trading in a 27.50-28.50 range against the U.S. dollar in the future.
His statement follows last week's managed float of the baht by Thai authorities and the setting of a daily baht/dollar reference rate by the central bank.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium was quoted at 35/55 satangs per dollar offshore and 24/30 in the domestic market.
The overnight interbank rate fell to 17-18 percent from 23-25 in the morning as banks lent out their surplus funds after the passing of reserve requirement, dealers said.
All commercial banks have to meet the central bank's reserve deadline on seventh and 22nd of each month.
